title: Which traffic Bandwidth Control covers: locations and limits

prose.text: Rules are only half of Bandwidth Control; the location decides whether a flow is shaped and against what total. {{limits-per-location}} {{known-locations-only}}

prose.label: Sublocations.
prose.text: Whether a sublocation shares its location's limits, holds its own, or is exempt, and how the parent and child limits must relate, is in [[zia.locations.bandwidth]]; the Bandwidth Control consequence is that a sublocation in the default shared mode shares its location's limits ([[zia.locations.bandwidth]], claim shared-by-default). {{guest-wifi}}

prose.label: Sizing the limits.
prose.text: {{sizing}} The vendor's overhead figure is stated inconsistently {{divergence:overhead-percentage}}.

checks.do: Whether the location's Enforce Bandwidth Control switch is on and its maximums are set, since rules do not shape its traffic otherwise.
Each sublocation's mode, since a sublocation in the shared mode shares its location's limits.
Whether the traffic comes from a configured location rather than a remote user, which these limits do not cover.

limits-per-location.statement: Bandwidth Control starts with maximum upload and download limits per location, which apply to traffic proxied to Zscaler. These limits are required before the class-based rules (the second level) can be used.

quotes: You can configure maximum upload and download bandwidth limits for each location in your organization.
These limits apply to the traffic that is proxied to Zscaler for Bandwidth Control.
You must configure upload and download bandwidth limits for your locations or sublocations to use the second level of bandwidth controls.

known-locations-only.statement: Bandwidth controls apply to traffic from configured locations only. They do not apply to remote users, whose traffic does not come from a configured location and whose source IP has unknown upload and download bandwidth.

quotes: The service applies bandwidth controls to traffic from known locations only
The Bandwidth Control policy does not apply to remote users because their traffic does not come from a configured location

enforce-toggle.statement: A location's Bandwidth Control section has an Enforce Bandwidth Control switch plus Download and Upload maximums in Mbps.

quotes: Enforce Bandwidth Control: Enable to enforce Bandwidth Control for the location.
Download (Mbps): Specify the maximum bandwidth limit.

toggle-gates-rules.statement: Bandwidth Control rules therefore shape a location's traffic only where that location enforces Bandwidth Control and has limits; with the switch off, rules and classes for that location have no effect.
toggle-gates-rules.conditions: Derived from the toggle's description and the requirement for limits; no source states the outcome of a rule for a location with the toggle off.

guest-wifi.statement: Enforcing fixed limits on a sublocation is described as particularly useful for guest Wi-Fi networks.

quotes: Enforcing limits is particularly useful for guest Wi-Fi networks.

sizing.statement: Location limits should leave out UDP traffic sent to Zscaler and traffic not forwarded to Zscaler, should exclude TCP overhead, and are best set to 70-80% of the location's overall bandwidth.
sizing.conditions: The overhead figure is stated two ways in the same article; see the divergence.

quotes: Ensure that you exclude UDP traffic sent to Zscaler and traffic not forwarded to Zscaler while specifying the limits.
Only 70–80% of the overall bandwidth per location is the ideal setting for upload and download limits.

overhead-percentage.summary: How much of a location's bandwidth to subtract as TCP overhead

quotes: About 5–7% of TCP traffic is overhead, such as packet headers. The Zscaler service does not include these in its bandwidth calculations. It only includes the application traffic.

positions.says: About 5-7% of TCP traffic is overhead that the service leaves out of its bandwidth calculations.

quotes: (Actual bandwidth) – (10–15% overhead) = Upload and Download bandwidth

positions.says: The sizing equation subtracts 10-15% overhead from actual bandwidth.

overhead-percentage.impact: A limit computed with the wrong overhead is off by several percent of the link; use the 70-80% guidance as the planning point and treat the exact overhead as unresolved.

sublocation-share-detail.title: How shared sublocation bandwidth is divided under contention
sublocation-share-detail.detail: How a sublocation share of its location bandwidth interacts with rule minimums and maximums, both in [[zia.locations.bandwidth]] sharing and under Override, is not described by the captured pages.
